title: Sensex, Nifty Week Ahead: Jio IPO, Q2 Earnings, Crude and FII Flows in Focus
excerpt: After a 3.11% Sensex rally to 74,729.27, a holiday-shortened week brings India's largest IPO, a packed Q2 earnings calendar, RBI minutes and China GDP — with Brent near $110 and FII selling still to absorb.
body:
• Sensex closed last week at 74,729.27, up 3.11%, and the Nifty at 23,146.15, up 2.78% — their biggest weekly gain since April, led by a surge of more than 10% in IT stocks.
  • Jio Platforms' Rs 30,213 crore IPO — India's largest ever — opens Wednesday, October 21 and closes Friday, October 23, at a price band of Rs 1,065–Rs 1,119; anchor bidding is on Monday, October 19.
  • Trading is shut Tuesday, October 20 for Dussehra; Q2 results from Infosys, Bajaj Finance, Kotak Mahindra Bank and UltraTech Cement will drive stock-specific moves.
  • Watch Nifty support at 22,500 and resistance near 23,500, Brent crude near $110 a barrel, and whether FII selling — Rs 8,991 crore last week, the ninth straight week of outflows — eases further.

Indian equities start the week of October 19–23 after their strongest weekly advance in six months, facing a concentrated test: India's largest-ever IPO, a heavy slate of September-quarter earnings, crude near $110 a barrel and a ninth straight week of foreign selling to absorb.

The BSE Sensex ended last week at 74,729.27, up 2,256.94 points or 3.11%, while the NSE Nifty 50 closed at 23,146.15, up 625.7 points or 2.77%, according to Outlook Money's week-ahead preview. IT stocks led after results from TCS, HCLTech and Tech Mahindra beat or met estimates — Tech Mahindra's profit rose 32.7% to Rs 1,586 crore. The advance was narrow: Bank Nifty finished nearly flat at 55,844, and FMCG, real estate and pharma ended lower.

Jio IPO will test market liquidity

The centrepiece is the Jio Platforms IPO. The Reliance-backed company opens its issue Wednesday, October 21 and closes it Friday, October 23, with anchor bidding Monday, October 19. The offer is a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares at Rs 1,065–Rs 1,119, with no offer-for-sale component, raising Rs 30,213 crore — ahead of Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870 crore issue in 2024 as India's largest IPO.

At the top of the band the issue values Jio at about Rs 10.3 lakh crore; the minimum application is 12 shares, or Rs 13,428. About Rs 27,500 crore of proceeds will repay loans, according to Mint's Plain Facts preview. Allotment is expected October 26, with listing on October 28.

"Liquidity is about to be tested by the Jio IPO, while crude, FII flows and bond yields remain the forces that will decide whether this recovery has legs. One strong week is a start, not a trend."

— Sarvam Goel, Founder, Pocketful

Q2 earnings broaden beyond IT

The September-quarter season gathers pace, and the question is whether profit growth spreads beyond technology. Reporting this week: Infosys, Bajaj Finance, Kotak Mahindra Bank, UltraTech Cement, Hindustan Zinc, Union Bank of India, IREDA, Coforge, Swiggy, Tata Motors, HPCL and the Adani energy companies. Weekend results from HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis Bank — all reporting higher profits — will set Monday's tone for financials.

Infosys will be judged on its FY27 revenue guidance of 1.5–3%, Bajaj Finance on credit quality, UltraTech on volumes against higher fuel costs, and HPCL on refining margins.

FII selling, crude and the rupee

FIIs remained net sellers for a ninth straight week, but selling eased sharply to Rs 8,991 crore from Rs 30,294 crore the previous week, and FIIs turned buyers of Rs 1,166 crore on Friday. Domestic institutions bought Rs 7,813 crore; month-to-date, DII buying of Rs 48,168 crore has almost fully absorbed FII selling of Rs 48,769 crore, Bajaj Broking noted.

Brent crude is the main external risk, surging more than 5% last week toward $110 a barrel — a level that lifts India's import bill. Against that, the rupee strengthened nearly 2%, its biggest weekly gain in seven months, to Rs 94.96 per dollar. Forex reserves, due Friday, had fallen to $726 billion in the week ended October 9 as the RBI sold dollars. The US 10-year yield near 5.09% remains a headwind, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

Macro data and technical levels

China's Q3 GDP, due Monday, follows growth of 4.3% in April–June — the weakest in more than three years — against Beijing's 4.5–5% target. The RBI releases its October MPC minutes on Wednesday, October 21; the committee raised the repo rate 25 basis points to 5.5% unanimously but split 4–2 on shifting to a calibrated tightening stance. US jobless claims follow Thursday (200,000 expected, against 199,000 previously) and US flash PMI readings land Friday, alongside India's flash PMI.

Technically, Bajaj Broking sees the pullback extending toward 23,500 if momentum holds; failure to sustain last week's high would leave the Nifty consolidating between 22,500 and 23,150, with 22,500 the key support. For investors holding India exposure, the week is a levels-and-liquidity test: earnings breadth, Jio demand and crude will decide whether the two-week, roughly 950-point Nifty recovery broadens.
